extracted.intended_audience: emerging and submitted short-story writers from Commonwealth countries; prize judges and administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Judging criteria and procedural rules for the Commonwealth Short Story Prize, aimed at assessing unpublished short fiction by writers from Commonwealth countries and elevating underrepresented emerging voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original Voices
rubrics_metrics.description: "Original voices that reflect diverse experiences across the Commonwealth." Originality is dual: linguistic distinctiveness AND lived-experience distinctiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges seek voices that are not merely imitative of dominant literary traditions but show distinct language use and perspectives shaped by the writer's experience. Originality includes both how the story is told (voice/language) and what experience it communicates. Avoid polished mimicry of Anglo-American idioms when it erases local distinctiveness; conversely, avoid fetishizing 'difference' as the whole of originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity and Depth Across Genres
rubrics_metrics.description: The prize is genre-open. Literary, speculative, romantic, historical — all eligible if executed with creativity and depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genre alone is not a disqualifier; judges evaluate whether the chosen genre is used with imaginative risk and substantive depth. Surface genre tropes without deeper exploration count poorly. Stories should demonstrate both inventive idea (creativity) and layered meaning or emotional/intellectual weight (depth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of Experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit value placed on perspectives outside the Anglo-American literary mainstream. Cultural specificity is an asset, not a liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries that convey culturally specific contexts, ways of seeing, and concerns are positively valued. The prize rewards perspectives that expand the canon rather than reinforcing familiar metropolitan viewpoints. Anti-pattern: treating cultural markers as exotic props rather than embedding them authentically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility to Newer Writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Particularly aimed at writers with "little or no work published." Established writers are not the target. The prize values the not-yet-recognized voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is given to emerging authors; submission pools and judging are structured to surface fresh talent. Judges may weigh the potential and distinctiveness of a previously unpublished or minimally published writer more favorably than a technically accomplished piece by an already-established author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous judging
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymous judging — judges evaluate without knowing author identity (mitigates known-name bias).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author names and identifying details are removed during evaluation to promote impartiality. This is a procedural safeguard intended to focus assessment on the text alone rather than reputation or publication history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial screening and longlist process
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial screening by reader team; Longlist of 200 → International judging panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A multi-stage selection: reader-team filters entries to a longlist, then regional and international judges assess longlisted stories. Awareness of these stages helps entrants understand that early-stage readers apply filtering criteria (readability, fit, basic craft) before deeper judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional judging structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Five regional judges (one each from Africa; Asia; Canada and Europe; Caribbean; Pacific). Each regional judge focuses on stories from their region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional judges bring contextual knowledge to evaluate cultural specificity and local voice. This structure aims to reduce misreading of culturally particular elements and to ensure fair representation across regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count eligibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should conform to the stated length range; entries outside this range risk disqualification or lower consideration. The range indicates the expected narrative scope and compression judges will assume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication status eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Unpublished short fiction (some flexibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primarily for unpublished work; minor flexibility exists but submitting published pieces may jeopardize eligibility. Check specific entry rules for allowable prior appearances/format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Written by a citizen of any Commonwealth country (56 nations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must meet the citizenship requirement; this is a core eligibility constraint defining the prize's geographic/community scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Translated entries accepted (with translator credit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories originally in other languages may be submitted in translation, but translators must be credited. Judges will consider translation quality as part of craft evaluation when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity of place
rubrics_metrics.description: Specificity of place — locality grounded in concrete detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners and shortlisted stories frequently anchor narrative in tangible, local detail that makes setting credible and vivid. Vagueness or generic settings that could be anywhere are weaker; specificity should illuminate character and theme rather than serve as mere ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional speech and voice without exoticizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice that reflects regional speech without exoticizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective stories convey local speech rhythms and idioms authentically while avoiding caricature or reduction to 'colorful' dialect. Anti-pattern: using dialect or speech markers solely to signal otherness or entertain readers unfamiliar with the region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with contemporary social conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement with contemporary social conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that dialog with current social, political, or cultural realities of the writer's context are valued. Engagement can be direct or subtle but should show an awareness of lived circumstances rather than nostalgic or ahistorical depictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary craft at international standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary craft (structural unity, language precision) at international standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges look for strong structural coherence, precise and effective language, and polished narrative technique. Technical weaknesses (plot holes, uneven pacing, careless prose) undermine chances even if voice or originality is strong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of 'single-story' stereotyping
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoidance of "single-story" stereotyping of the writer's region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should resist reductive narratives that present a region or people as monolithic. Judges favor complexity and multiplicity of representation over familiar tropes that confirm outside prejudices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of voice (assessment framing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticity of voice (regional / cultural specificity without exoticism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing authenticity, judges consider whether voice arises organically from character and context. Forced or performative 'authenticity' that reads as imitation is penalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality (assessment framing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality — does this voice add to what exists?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond novelty of plot, judges ask whether the work contributes new perspectives, narrative approaches, or linguistic textures to conversations about Commonwealth literatures. Derivative or predictable treatments score lower.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth (intellectual and emotional weight)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depth — intellectual and emotional weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should offer resonance: thematic complexity, emotional truth, or insight that lingers beyond the reading. Lightweight or purely performative pieces without underlying stakes are less competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre fitness
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre fitness (whatever genre is chosen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within its genre, a story should meet or subvert genre expectations convincingly. Misapplied genre conventions or shallow pastiche weaken assessment; conversely, thoughtful subversion that serves thematic aims is rewarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with the writer's actual context
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement with the writer's actual context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges value work that reflects knowledge of the writer's social/cultural environment in ways that enrich the story. Superficial signifiers of context without deeper integration into character and plot are criticized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prize ideological orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prize values emerging voices from underrepresented regions rather than privileging craft mastery in established writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection criteria are intentionally oriented toward amplifying underrepresented writers; entrants and judges should be aware that this ideological axis (emergence & representation) informs evaluation alongside craft. This distinguishes the prize from others that prioritize established reputations or pure technical mastery.
